listenings.text: Hi Bev, it's Dana Reid, Renato's coach. I've got some great news for you. Renato's quarterfinal was surfed this afternoon, and he won it! Nobody expected it. He was the underdog, and Finn Carter, the local boy, was in the lead for most of the heat. Then, in the last minute, Renato caught a beautiful wave, and it was given an eight point one by the judges. That was the best score of the whole day. So he finished first, and he's in the semifinal. Finn advanced too, in second place. The other two boys were eliminated. After the heat, Renato was interviewed for the club newsletter, and I think his photo was taken about a hundred times! We're driving back to Perth tonight, so we'll be home at about nine. He's tired, and he's very hungry. Okay, see you later. Bye!

Jess, it's Kai again. Okay, are you sitting down? Renato won! I'm serious. With four minutes left, Ethan got a six, so Renato was in third place for about a minute. I was so nervous. Then the last set came, and Renato was in the perfect spot. He did three big turns, and the crowd went crazy. The horn was blown two seconds after he finished. Then the scores were read out on the speakers: eight point one! Finn shook his hand. He was really nice about it. And Dana was almost crying. A picture of Renato with the whole squad was posted on the club page ten minutes ago. Go and look! Okay, we're going to celebrate with some pizza now. Bye!

reading.rtitle: Underdog Wins the Biggest Upset of the Day
paras: The first round of the Interschool Surf Series was held at Margaret River on Sunday. Sixty-four young surfers from twelve schools were invited. In the morning, the heats were surfed in small, clean waves. In the afternoon, the wind changed and the conditions became unpredictable.

The biggest upset of the day was seen in the second Under 16 quarterfinal. Finn Carter, a local surfer and last year's winner, was beaten by Renato Lara, a fifteen-year-old exchange student from Brazil. Renato surfs for Scarborough High, and he is coached by Dana Reid.

For most of the heat, Finn was in the lead. Then there was a long lull. With one minute left, Renato was in third place. Then a big set came. Renato caught the last wave of the heat and did three strong turns. The wave was given an 8.10 by the judges, the highest score of the day. The crowd on the beach cheered loudly.

Renato finished first with 15.30 points, and Finn finished second with 13.50. Both surfers advanced to the semifinal. Ethan Moss and Noah Brooks were eliminated. After the heat, Renato celebrated with his teammates. "I was the underdog," he said. "Everybody was surprised, even me." The semifinals will be held later this month.
reading.source: Simulated club newsletter report, written for this lesson.
